notes: Interface size: Ctrl and + or −, Ctrl with the mouse wheel away from the files, or the menu's Interface size, make the window larger or smaller, from 50% to 200%; Ctrl+0 goes back to 100%. Ctrl and the wheel over the files still size the tiles. Menus and message boxes follow the window's size. Zooming in makes the window bigger if it would be too small for its layout, as far as the screen allows. The size is kept for this app on this PC.
The menu (⋯) has NorthRay Software's website, which opens Files' page on the website in your browser.
Buttons have Writing Studio's calm look: one style everywhere, a soft frame that lifts when you point at it, and a small icon beside the words where there's room.
Faint text is a little darker in the light theme and a little lighter in the dark one, so it reads easily (WCAG AA), and the light theme's green is deeper for the same reason.
Drag the edges of the column headings in Details to make the columns wider or narrower. The widths are remembered.
Each folder remembers its own view (Details, Icons or Gallery) and sort order. View › “Use this view and order for every folder” makes the current one the default everywhere.

Details shows how many items each folder holds and how big it is altogether, worked out in the background (very large folders show “over” a size after a few seconds). The status bar shows the same for a selected folder. Press F5 to work them out again.

Pictures fade in as they're made instead of popping in, and they're kept on disk (in your local app data, up to about 300 MB) so folders you've seen before show their pictures at once. Menu › “Clear saved thumbnails” deletes them.
Long copies and moves show how far they've got inside the window, as well as in Windows' own progress window.

Quick look: press Space to see the selected file large over the window: a picture at full size with its pixel size, the start of a text file, or its icon. Space or Esc closes it, the arrow keys move to the next file and the look follows, and Enter opens it. (Ctrl+Space still shows or hides the preview pane.)
Hold Ctrl and turn the mouse wheel in Icons view to make the icons and pictures bigger or smaller. The size is remembered.
Drag the sidebar's edge to make it wider or narrower. The width is remembered.
A › after each part of the folder path opens a list of the folders inside it, to jump straight there. Backspace goes up a folder.
The status bar shows a picture's size in pixels when one picture is selected, and extensions in Details are drawn fainter so the names stand out.
Moving more than 50 items to the Recycle Bin asks first.

Rename many files at once: select them, right-click and choose “Rename these together” (or Ctrl+Shift+F2). Build the new names from {name} (the name now), {n} (a number, with a start and a number of digits), {date} (the day it was last changed) and {folder} (the folder's name), find and replace within them, and change them to lower case, UPPER CASE or Title Case. Extensions are kept unless you choose to change them too.

Every new name is previewed before anything happens, and names that can't be used (already taken, given twice, or not allowed by Windows) are shown in red and stop the rename. Renames that depend on each other, such as 1 to 2 and 2 to 3, or two names swapped, are done in an order that never overwrites anything.
Ctrl+Z puts the old names back after a batch rename, and colour labels, tags and collections follow the new names. If a rename fails part-way, the names already changed are put back.
Fixed: buttons in question boxes (such as “Delete permanently?”) didn't respond to clicks when Windows' display scaling was above 100%.

The sidebar fits short windows and large display scaling: the places, collections and labels scroll with the mouse wheel instead of running into the item count at the bottom, and the folder tree keeps room of its own.

The Recycle Bin opens inside Files: what's in it, where each thing was deleted from and when, with Restore and Delete permanently (right-click, the Delete key, or the preview pane) and Empty the Recycle Bin. It uses Windows' own Recycle Bin, so it matches File Explorer; its right-click menu in the sidebar still offers File Explorer's view. If Windows doesn't list what's in it, Files says so and offers File Explorer.

Drag and drop with other programs: drag files out of Files into any program that takes files from File Explorer (an email, a chat, an art program), and drop files from File Explorer or the desktop onto a folder, a pane, a collection or the sidebar in Files. Moves and copies follow File Explorer's rules (Ctrl copies, Shift moves).
Colour labels: right-click anything and choose a colour (or pick one in the preview pane). It shows as a bar beside its name in Details and a dot in Icons and Gallery views.

Tags: give files and folders as many tags as you like from the right-click menu or the preview pane, and take them off again. The sidebar's Tags button lists every tag; choosing one shows everything with it.
Search by label: tag:dragon (or #dragon), tag:"two words", colour:red, mixed with the other search words. The colour dots in the sidebar do the same in one click.

Collections: groups of files and folders from anywhere, without moving them. Make one from the sidebar or from “Add to collection”, drag things onto it, open it like a folder (the Folder column says where each thing really is), and rename or delete it from its right-click menu. Things that have gone missing are shown as missing.
Gallery view (Ctrl+Shift+1 or the toolbar): big square pictures for art folders, the name over the picture when you point at it.

Labels and collections are kept in NorthRay Files' own file, so the files themselves are never changed. They follow things renamed, moved or deleted in NorthRay Files; things moved by another program lose them.
Long submenus (such as a long list of tags) have a search field too.
A preview pane (Alt+P, the toolbar button or the menu): the selected file's picture, or the start of a text file, with its type, size and date, and Open. Several selected: how many and their size.
Pictures of art files in Icons view and the preview pane: Photoshop (.psd and .psb, from the picture Photoshop saves with the file), Procreate, Krita (.kra) and OpenRaster (.ora).
Videos and PDFs show the picture Windows' own thumbnail handlers make, as in File Explorer, where Windows has one for that kind of file.
From search results, “Open its folder” in the preview pane goes to where a result is, with it selected.

Search: type in the search box (Ctrl+F or F3) and results come straight away from the folder and every folder in it, with a Folder column saying where each one is. More letters narrow the results instantly; Esc goes back to the folder.
Search for a phrase in quotes, wildcards (*.png), a kind of file (kind:picture, video, music, document, archive or folder) or an extension (ext:psd, or just .psd).
“Search the whole PC” asks the Windows Search index, as File Explorer does. If Windows Search isn't available, Files says so and reads the drives instead.
Search results can be opened, copied, cut, renamed, deleted and dragged like anything else.
Long pop-up menus have a search field and scroll.
Tabs: Ctrl+T opens one, Ctrl+W closes it, Ctrl+Tab moves between them, and “Open in a new tab” is in a folder's right-click menu.
Two panes side by side (Ctrl+\ or the toolbar button), each with its own tabs; F6 moves between them, and “Copy to” or “Move to the other pane” is in the right-click menu.
Drag and drop: drag files onto a folder or into the other pane to move them (hold Ctrl to copy; between drives they are copied, as in File Explorer).
Pinned folders: drag a folder to the sidebar, or choose “Pin to the sidebar”; right-click a pinned folder to unpin it.
A folder tree under This PC: open a drive or folder with its arrow, and it opens itself to the folder you're in.
Your tabs, panes and pinned folders are there again next time you open Files.

Copy, cut and paste (Ctrl+C, Ctrl+X, Ctrl+V), and in the right-click menu. It works both ways with File Explorer. A copy in the same folder is named “cover - Copy.png”, as in File Explorer, and what arrives is selected.
Rename in place (F2): the name without its extension is selected, and a name Windows can't use is explained instead of failing.
New folder (Ctrl+Shift+N), named as you make it.
Delete moves things to the Recycle Bin; Shift+Delete deletes them for good, after asking. The Recycle Bin is in the sidebar with how many items it holds, to open or empty.
All of this goes through Windows' own file operations, so its progress, “replace or skip” and Recycle Bin work as in File Explorer.
“More options” (and Shift+F10) opens Windows' own right-click menu for the selected items: Open with, Send to, Properties and the rest.
Folders refresh by themselves when anything in them changes, here or in another program, keeping your place and selection.
Messages and questions (“Delete this?”, “Saved”) now appear in a NorthRay dialog that matches the app, instead of the plain grey Windows box.
Text on the night sky stays clear: stars keep away from the words in title bars and sidebars.
The stars in the night sky twinkle softly (still when Windows' animations are turned off).
Fixed: a button that opens a menu or dialog could, rarely, act on the wrong thing.
No more status bar along the bottom of the window. Messages appear for a moment as a small note near the bottom instead. How many items are here, and what's selected, are at the foot of the sidebar.

Minimise, maximise and close are now part of the app's own top area, like NorthRay Browser: they sit at the end of the toolbar, instead of a separate Windows title bar. Drag the empty part of the top to move the window; double-click it to maximise. On Windows 11, pointing at maximise shows the snap layouts.
Pictures now show the image itself in Icons view: JPEG, PNG, GIF, BMP, TIFF and icon files, plus WebP, HEIC and AVIF where Windows has their codecs.
Phone and camera photos are turned the right way up, and pictures are never stretched.
Bigger tiles in Icons view. Pictures are made in the background, the ones on screen first, so big folders stay quick.
Online-only files (OneDrive and similar) keep their normal icon, so browsing never downloads them.
First preview: browse folders and drives with a NorthRay sidebar, a breadcrumb address bar, and Details and Icons views with Windows' own icons.
Sort, select with the mouse and keyboard, type a name to jump to it, and open files in their usual app.
Read-only for now: nothing is copied, moved, renamed or deleted. Those come in the next version.
